subject: Draft MAP: cost sensitivity, caching & burst assumptions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@curopath.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP: cost sensitivity, caching & burst assumptions

Hi Elaine —

Attached is a first-pass MAP section focused on the unit-econ checks you asked for (tokens / $ baseline, expected caching hits, and burst coverage). The two files are: CuroPath_MAP_Draft_v2.docx (MAP + milestones) and cost_model_sheet.xlsx (tokenization samples + baseline calc).

Quick callouts we put in the draft:
- Baseline token rate: 1.9 tokens per character (sampled from the pilot prompts you shared)
- Default billing unit: per 1,000 tokens; we show tokens/$ with both hosted and dedicated rate scenarios
- Caching assumptions: 25% prefix-cache hit expected for autocomplete flows, 60% for static templates (we marked these with confidence levels)
- Batching: we recommend a 50ms window for interactive UI to group small requests into micro-batches; for async jobs we show 2–5 request batch sizes
- Burst capacity: suggested reserved buffer to cover 3x p95 QPS for 72 hours while we scale Dedicated pool if needed

Can you confirm these assumptions line-by-line? Specifically:
1) Are we comfortable with the 1.9 tokens/char baseline for your datasets, or should we use a separate sample?
2) For caching, which paths have strict cache-staleness requirements (seconds vs minutes)?
3) Any internal limit on batching latency we should respect (e.g., max client-side wait of 100ms)?

If these look good I’ll fold your answers into the MAP and flag the items that would affect pricing (token rate, caching hit rate, and burst SLAs).

Thanks —
Ben
--
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: cost sensitivity, caching & burst assumptions

Ben —

Thanks for the draft. A few clarifications from my side after a quick pass:
- Token baseline: our current internal tokenizer metrics vary by model; 1.9 tokens/char sounds reasonable for the short prompts and UI completions, but our long-context analytics (document summarization) average closer to 3.1 tokens/char. Would you like a sample export of 500 typical prompts?
- Caching: we have two main patterns: (A) autocomplete (very high locality, prefix-based; updates on template deploys only) — TTL measured in minutes; (B) long-document embeddings & rerank (low cache hit). For (A) we can expect >40% cache hit once templates are warmed.
- Batching latency: product requires sub-120ms tail for interactive autocompletion. If batching pushes tail beyond that we need smaller batch windows or smart priority lanes.

Also: can you attach a stripped example of the eval logs you mentioned on our discovery call (token counts per call + latency distribution)? That will help us validate savings projections.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Turner
Director, ML Platforms — CuroPath
elaine.turner@curopath.com | +1 646-555-0987

Subject: RE: Draft MAP: cost sensitivity, caching & burst assumptions

Elaine / team —

Attaching a concise unit-econ summary (unit_econ_quickview.pdf) and past pilot logs stripped for PII. Key points:
- We ran your 500-sample export through two model flavors (open-variant v1 and opt-quant v2) and derived:
   * Interactive prompts (mean length ~160 chars): 1.8 tokens/char -> ~288 tokens/call
   * Docs summarize (mean length ~1,600 chars): 2.9 tokens/char -> ~4,640 tokens/call
- Suggested billing model lines in MAP (conservative / typical / optimistic) shown with tokens/$ calculus. Example: hosted baseline = $0.012 / 1k tokens (conservative) -> interactive ~ $0.0035 / call
- Caching effect: concrete recommendation: enable prefix caching for autocomplete endpoints with an expected steady-state 35–45% hit (we modeled both 35% and 45% in the sheet). 35% hit reduces tokens billed by ~22% overall for mixed traffic.
- Batching policy we recommend: 30ms micro-batch for UI (keeps 95th tail < 110ms in our microbench) and 250ms batching for background bulk requests where throughput matters more than latency.
- Burst buffer: propose a 2x reserved buffer for initial rollout (30 days), then re-evaluate using telemetry. We also included a rapid scale playbook if 3x p95 sustained.

If that aligns, Ben will merge into the MAP doc and we’ll produce a small addendum that lists the five pricing-sensitive checkpoints for the procurement team.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: unit_econ_quickview.pdf (summary), pilot_logs_stripped.csv (log sample)

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: cost sensitivity, caching & burst assumptions

Rachel / Ben —

This is very helpful and closer to what our procurement and infra folks need to sign off. A couple of operational constraints and asks from our side before we lock the numbers into the MAP:
1) Acceptance criteria: we need a canary run with representative traffic for 7 days where unit-econ drift is <10% vs the pilot projection. Can you define the telemetry we will use to evaluate that (metrics + dashboards)?
2) SLA for burst: our infra team requires 99.5% coverage of p95 for planned launch windows. We can accept temporary credits if fallback occurs, but need clear escalation steps.
3) Doc/contract redline: our legal team asks that any pricing adjustments tied to cache-hit % be reviewed quarterly.

Also looping in Samir (ops) who will take the technical lead on the canary. Samir — we’d like to schedule the canary for the week of Aug 7 if possible. Can your team confirm capacity?

Thanks —
Elaine

Subject: RE: Draft MAP: cost sensitivity, caching & burst assumptions — Consolidated action items

Elaine / Samir —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the canary ask — we’ve consolidated everything into MAP_action_items_consolidated.docx and called out five pricing-sensitive checkpoints for procurement: token baseline, cache-hit measurement, canary duration & telemetry, burst SLA & crediting, and quarterly review window. High-level plan below (also in the doc):
- By 2028-07-20: Redwood to deliver telemetry dashboard template and the exact metric definitions (tokens_billed, cache_hit_rate, per_call_latency_p95). (Owner: Rachel)
- By 2028-07-27: CuroPath to provide a 500-sample export for long-context prompts and confirm acceptance criteria (Owner: Elaine)
- Week of 2028-08-07: 7-day canary (Owner: Samir + Redwood infra)
- By 2028-08-21: Post-canary reconciliation and final pricing adjustments if drift >10% (Owners: Procurement + Redwood)
- Contract milestone: sign-off on MAP and DocuSign (we’ll send the link).

Notes on cost impact (summary): 35% cache hit -> ~22% billed token reduction for mixed traffic; switching to Dedicated with our recommended quantized model reduces unit cost by another ~28% in our conservative scenario. Exact numbers are in the consolidated sheet.

Next steps: I’ll upload the final MAP and send a DocuSign link to the procurement contact once we get your confirmation on the sample export timing. Can we lock a 30-minute check on Wednesday 2028-07-18 at 11:00am PT to confirm dashboard metrics?

Thanks —
Ben
